phase_2d_correction.original_conclusion: Motor fires in wrong direction — cannot produce retrograde thrust
phase_2d_correction.corrected_conclusion: Motor fires in correct direction (nose-directed). During tail-first descent, nose-directed thrust IS retrograde braking. The Phase 2d test measured a rocket on the launch pad (ascending), not during tail-first descent.
phase_2d_correction.error_source: Phase 2d test used a minimal vehicle starting from rest. The +35.5 m/s velocity change was the rocket launching upward — not relevant to tail-first braking.

k550w_analysis.explanation: Motor fires during ascent (before apex at 8.513s). Adds energy, pushes booster higher. Longer fall from greater height. Net effect: lower impact speed than free descent (14.76 vs 21.70 m/s) but not braking during descent.

h180w_analysis.explanation: Same pattern — motor fires during ascent, adds energy. Higher impact speed than K550W because less energy added (smaller motor).

real_bottleneck.primary: Motor fires during ASCENT (before apex at 8.513s), not during descent. To brake, motor must fire AFTER apex when vz < 0.
real_bottleneck.secondary: Even with post-apogee ignition, horizontal speed (19.04 m/s) limits total touchdown speed. Vertical-only braking cannot reduce total speed below sqrt(0 + 19.04^2) = 19.04 m/s.
real_bottleneck.tertiary: The tail-first window is 35s long (8.5s to 43.7s), but the motor must fire within a specific sub-window where both: (a) vz < 0 (descending), and (b) theta > 0 (tail-first).
real_bottleneck.recommendation: Test delays > 9s (after apex) to find the actual braking regime. Also investigate whether the motor's horizontal thrust component can reduce horizontal speed.
